* agent

** agent_cancel

Stop a subagent you spawned.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent cancel=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id returned by agent_spawn |

** agent_list

List the agent definitions available to spawn, and every task currently known with its state.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent list=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

Takes no arguments.

** agent_models

List the models a provider offers, for use as agent_spawn's model argument. The value to pass is "provider/model".

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent models=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =provider= | string | yes | Provider name, from agent_providers |

** agent_providers

List the AI providers this cmacs can reach, and whether each looks usable. Use before agent_models when you want to pick a model for a spawn.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent providers=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

Takes no arguments.

** agent_result

Collect what a subagent produced. Call it once agent_status reports `done'; on a `failed' task it returns whatever was produced before the failure, which is usually the explanation. For an agent you have sent more than one message to, this returns the answer to the most recent one. Pass `turn' to read an earlier one, or use agent_log to read the whole exchange.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent result=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id returned by agent_spawn |
| =turn= | integer | no | Which turn's reply to read; omit for the latest |

** agent_spawn

Hand a piece of work to another agent, which runs in parallel with you. Returns a task id immediately -- it does NOT wait for the work to finish. Poll it with agent_status and collect the answer with agent_result once the state is `done'. Spawn several and poll them all rather than spawning one and waiting.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent spawn=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, confirm=ask

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =task= | string | yes | What the subagent should do. Write it as a standalone instruction: the subagent does not see your conversation. |
| =agent= | string | no | Which agent definition to use; omit for the default |
| =model= | string | no | Model as provider/model, e.g. claude/claude-sonnet-4-6. Omit to use the agent's own -- call agent_models first if you want to choose one. |
| =title= | string | no | Short label for the dashboard |

** agent_status

Check on a subagent you spawned. States are draft, queued, starting, running, waiting-input, done, failed, cancelled and over-budget. Only `done' and `failed' are final.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool agent status=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id returned by agent_spawn |

* ai

** ai_call

Send PROMPT to an AI provider and return the final answer. Like ai_prompt, but with 'tools':true the model is given the built-in agent tools (bash/read/write/edit/glob/grep/ls/web_fetch) and runs a multi-turn tool loop on a worker thread. Optional 'provider' / 'system' / 'model' behave as for ai_prompt.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai call=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, async (timeout 1800s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai call --prompt 'What is in ./README.org?' --tools=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =prompt= | string | yes | User prompt |
| =provider= | string | no | Provider name |
| =system= | string | no | System prompt |
| =model= | string | no | Model name |
| =tools= | boolean | no | Give the model the built-in agent tools |

** ai_embed_similarity

Cosine similarity of two texts' embeddings, in [-1, 1]: 1 is the same direction, 0 unrelated, -1 opposite. Use it to judge whether two passages mean the same thing -- near-duplicate detection, or checking an answer against a source. Needs a local embedding provider (ollama). Optional 'model' overrides the default embedding model. To SEARCH the notes corpus use memory_search instead; this compares two specific strings.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai embed-similarity=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: async (timeout 120s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai embed-similarity --a 'a cat' --b 'a kitten'=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =a= | string | yes | First text |
| =b= | string | yes | Second text |
| =model= | string | no | Embedding model |

** ai_lql

Run an LQL query on the libresearch server and return its rows (at most 100 shown). LQL pipes search results: search "glib", category: CODE | filter extra.stars > 100 | fields title, url -- or the shorthand gtk docs | filter site("docs.gtk.org"). 'explain' returns the plan without running it. An invalid query reports the server's position and caret excerpt.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai lql=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: async (timeout 120s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai lql --query 'gtk docs | filter site("docs.gtk.org")'=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =query= | string | yes | LQL query |
| =explain= | boolean | no | Plan without running |

Open a cmacs-ai chat buffer. If PROMPT is given, the prompt is sent as the first user turn and streamed. Optional 'model' overrides the provider's default model. Returns the buffer name.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai open-chat=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai open-chat --provider claude=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =prompt= | string | no | Optional initial prompt |
| =provider= | string | no | Provider name |
| =model= | string | no | Model name |

** ai_prompt

Send PROMPT to an AI provider via cmacs-ai and return its answer. Optional 'provider' (claude / openai / gemini / grok / ollama / claude-code / opencode / claude-tmux / grok-build / antigravity / cursor) overrides the default; optional 'system' is a system prompt; optional 'model' overrides the provider's default model.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai prompt=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, async (timeout 600s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai prompt --prompt 'Name three GLib main-loop sources'=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =prompt= | string | yes | User prompt |
| =provider= | string | no | Provider name |
| =system= | string | no | System prompt |
| =model= | string | no | Model name |

** ai_research

Research a question on the web with libresearch and return a cited answer: the answer with numbered citations [n], then the sources (title, URL). Needs a libresearch server (cmacs-ai-libresearch-url). 'deep' lets the server run follow-up searches; 'pages' (1-20) is how many pages it reads. A run takes minutes.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai research=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: async (timeout 960s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai research --question 'What changed in wlroots 0.20?'=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =question= | string | yes | The question |
| =deep= | boolean | no | Run follow-up searches |
| =pages= | integer | no | Pages to read, 1-20 |

** ai_web_fetch

Read a web page's text through libresearch (the server applies its own SSRF guard). 'archive' is never (default), fallback (use the Wayback Machine when the live page fails) or only; 'max_chars' (100-1000000) caps the text. Returns title, URL, the archived copy if one stood in, then the text.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai web-fetch=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: async (timeout 120s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai web-fetch --url https://docs.gtk.org/glib/=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =url= | string | yes | Page URL |
| =archive= | string | no | Wayback Machine policy One of: never, fallback, only. |
| =max_chars= | integer | no | Longest text |

** generate_image

Generate an image from a text prompt and insert it into a cmacs buffer. In an Org buffer the image is attached to the current node and previewed inline; elsewhere it is saved under cmacs-ai-image-dir. Optional 'references' is a comma-separated list of input images to condition on, each PATH or PATH::ROLE (e.g. "logo.png::style,cat.jpg::subject") -- roles tell the model what each reference is for. Optional 'provider' (gemini / openai / grok), 'model', 'aspect' (e.g. 16:9), 'size' (e.g. 1024x1024) and 'quality'. Optional 'buffer' names the target buffer; the current one is used otherwise. Generation takes tens of seconds.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool ai generate-image=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, async (timeout 300s)
- Example :: =emacsctl tool ai generate-image --prompt 'a brass orrery' --aspect 16:9=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =prompt= | string | yes | What to depict |
| =references= | string | no | Comma-separated PATH or PATH::ROLE reference images |
| =provider= | string | no | gemini/openai/grok |
| =model= | string | no | Model id |
| =aspect= | string | no | Aspect ratio |
| =size= | string | no | Pixel size |
| =quality= | string | no | Quality level |
| =buffer= | string | no | Target buffer name |

** calc_convert_units

Evaluate EXPRESSION and convert it to UNITS; with no UNITS, reduce it to base SI. Knows CODATA physical constants (c, G, h, hbar, k, Nav, me, mp), so '2 * G * 1.989e30 kg / c^2' reduces to the Schwarzschild radius of the Sun in metres, and '60 mph' converts to 'm/s'.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool calc convert-units=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Example :: =emacsctl tool calc convert-units --expression '60 mph' --units m/s=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =expression= | string | yes | Expression with units, e.g. 60 mph |
| =units= | string | no | Target units, e.g. m/s; omit to reduce to base SI |

** calc_describe

Describe one calculator by NAME: its title, category, arguments, return value and documentation.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool calc describe=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Example :: =emacsctl tool calc describe --name bscall=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =name= | string | yes | Calculator name, e.g. bscall |

** calc_eval

Evaluate a calculator EXPRESSION numerically and return the result. Uses desktop-calculator semantics: '/' and '*' associate left to right (so 2/3*4 is 2.667), angles are radians, and symbolic constants fold (e^(i*pi) is -1). Arbitrary precision. All registered calculators are callable as functions, e.g. 'bscall(100,100,0.05,0.2,1)' or 'lorentz(0.9)'. Bad input is reported as an error rather than echoed back unevaluated.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool calc eval=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Example :: =emacsctl tool calc eval --expression 'sqrt(5/3*3^4)'=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =expression= | string | yes | Expression, e.g. sqrt(5/3*3^4) |

** calc_eval_symbolic

Evaluate a calculator EXPRESSION symbolically, permitting free variables. This is the computer-algebra path: deriv(x^3,x), integ(x^2,x), solve(x^2-4=0,x), taylor(sin(x),x,5), factor, expand. Use calc_eval instead when a number is wanted.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool calc eval-symbolic=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Example :: =emacsctl tool calc eval-symbolic --expression 'deriv(x^3, x)'=

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =expression= | string | yes | Expression, e.g. deriv(x^3 + sin(x), x) |

** calc_list

List the registered calculators, optionally only those in one CATEGORY (financial, physics, relativity, tax, ...). Each is callable as a function from calc_eval.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool calc list=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =category= | string | no | Category to filter by |

* data

** lql_query

Run an LQL query inside the editor and return the rows as a text table. LQL is a pipeline language: `fetch SOURCE | filter EXPR | fields a, b | sort a DESC | summarize n = count(), by: {a} | limit N'. Sources include files of any format (read "path"), git_log and the other git_* sources, exec, journal, coredumps, sql, Kubernetes, and the editor's own state: buffers, windows, processes, recentf, kill_ring, bookmarks, org_headings, and the user's org notes repository: notes (one row per file: para, scope, area, title, tags, created/updated, todos, backlinks), note_headings, note_links and note_properties. NULL is three-valued: test presence with is_not_null(x), never x != null. Call lql_sources for the full list. Read-only.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool data lql-query=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =query= | string | yes | The LQL query |
| =max_rows= | integer | no | Most rows to return (default 100) |

List every LQL source lql_query can fetch from, including the editor-state sources cmacs defines.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool data lql-sources=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

Takes no arguments.

** lql_unwatch

Remove one of your standing LQL queries, by the NAME you gave lql_watch.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool data lql-unwatch=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =name= | string | yes | The watch's name |

** lql_watch

Register a standing LQL query and be told when its result changes: "tell me when X". The query (same language and sources as lql_query) is re-run every EVERY seconds; the first result is the baseline, and after that you receive a message, with a diff, only when the result differs from the last one. Prefer this to calling lql_query in a loop. Give KEY, the column(s) identifying a row, to have changed rows told apart from removed-and-added ones. Write a query whose result is small and stable -- filter, summarize, sort -- because any difference fires. A watch is yours alone, you may hold only a few, and all of them are removed when your run ends. Registering under a NAME you already use replaces that watch.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool data lql-watch=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =name= | string | yes | A short name for the watch: letters, digits, - or _ |
| =query= | string | yes | The LQL query to watch |
| =every= | integer | no | Seconds between runs (default 120, minimum 30) |
| =key= | string | no | Column, or comma-separated columns, identifying a row |

** lql_watches

List your standing LQL queries: state, interval, row count, when each last ran and last changed, its last error, and any change you have not yet been told about.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool data lql-watches=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

Takes no arguments.

The macro recorder (Super+Alt+r). start records the person's keys, clicks, drags and scrolls; stop writes last-recording.c (and NAME.c) and replies `recorded NAME STEPS PATH'; cancel discards; status reports. Starting from here needs gowl's `input-recording' consent, because it watches the person's input; the screen is framed while it runs and password prompts are not recorded.

- Flags :: destructive

** gowl_start_recording

Record real keyboard and pointer input so a human demonstration can be turned into a procedure. Returns a token for gowl_drain_recording and gowl_stop_recording. Bounded: the ring holds at most max_events (older events are dropped and counted) and the recording stops itself after max_seconds. Requires gowl's `input-recording' config key, which is separate from send_keys and off by default. While it runs the screen is framed in red and Super+Shift+Escape stops it. Capture is suppressed on the lock screen and for windows on the deny list, but gowl CANNOT see a password field inside an ordinary window -- review a trace before storing or sharing it.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool gowl start-recording=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: json
- Flags :: destructive

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =max_seconds= | integer | no | Stop automatically after this many seconds (default 120, maximum 3600) |
| =max_events= | integer | no | Ring size in events (default 4096, maximum 100000) |

** gowl_stop_recording

Stop the recording and take the tail, in the same shape gowl_drain_recording returns. Stopping a recording that already stopped itself still returns its remaining events exactly once.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool gowl stop-recording=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: json
- Flags :: destructive

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =token= | string | yes | Token from gowl_start_recording |

* mailbox

** agent_close

Finish with an agent for good: drop anything still queued for it and release the conversation it was holding. Its log stays readable. Do this when you are done with a subagent you have been going back and forth with, so it is not holding a session open indefinitely.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool mailbox agent-close=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id, from agent_spawn |

** agent_drop

Remove a message you queued but no longer want delivered. Only works while it is still waiting -- a message already given to the agent cannot be taken back.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool mailbox agent-drop=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id, from agent_spawn |
| =index= | integer | no | Which queued message, from agent_inbox. Omit to clear the whole queue. |

** agent_inbox

List the messages queued for an agent that it has not yet been given. Use it to check whether something you sent has been picked up.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool mailbox agent-inbox=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id, from agent_spawn |

** agent_log

Read the full transaction log of any agent -- every message it was given, every reply, every tool it called, in order. You do NOT need to have spawned it. This is how you inspect an agent that is misbehaving: read its log and see what it actually did, rather than what it says it did. Use from_turn to read only what is new since you last looked.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool mailbox agent-log=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id of the agent to inspect |
| =from_turn= | integer | no | Only entries from this turn onward. Omit for all. |
| =kinds= | string | no | Comma-separated entry kinds to keep: message, reply, tool, state. Omit for all. |

** agent_send

Say something more to an agent. Works whether it is still running -- the message reaches it during its current turn when it can take one mid-turn, and otherwise when that turn ends -- or already finished, in which case it starts again with the same conversation and remembers everything from before. Returns immediately; poll with agent_status and collect with agent_result as usual.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool mailbox agent-send=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, confirm=ask

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =id= | string | yes | Task id, from agent_spawn |
| =message= | string | yes | What to say. It continues the existing conversation, so you do not need to repeat context you already gave it. |

List a document's blocks with the anchors needed to edit them. Each line is INDEX, then the heading level or slide number, then the text. Pass an INDEX back to office_set_text to change that block -- this is how you locate what to edit.

- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |

Read the text of a Word document, spreadsheet or presentation -- .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .odt, .ods or .odp. Returns the readable content: paragraphs for documents, tab-separated rows for spreadsheets, slide text for presentations. Use this instead of guessing at a file you cannot open.

- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =path= | string | yes | Absolute path to the document |

** office_set_cell

Set one spreadsheet cell and save the file. REF is like "Sheet1!B7", or just "B7" for the first sheet. A VALUE beginning with `=' is stored as a formula. Everything else in the document is preserved byte-for-byte.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool office set-cell=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, confirm=ask

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =path= | string | yes | Absolute path to the spreadsheet |
| =ref= | string | yes | Cell reference, e.g. Sheet1!B7 |
| =value= | string | yes | New value; a leading = makes it a formula |

** office_set_text

Replace the text of one block in a document, and save. INDEX comes from office_outline. For a presentation, pass the slide number as SLIDE too and INDEX is the shape's position on that slide. The block keeps its style; formatting that varied inside it is flattened. Nothing else in the document changes.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool office set-text=
- Surfaces :: mcp, menu, agents
- Returns :: string
- Flags :: destructive, confirm=ask

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =path= | string | yes | Absolute path to the document |
| =index= | integer | yes | Block index from office_outline |
| =text= | string | yes | Replacement text |
| =slide= | integer | no | Slide number, for presentations only |

Returns the QUEUED jobs with ids; the work runs asynchronously -- poll secondbrain_ingest_status until 'done' is true and read 'note_file'. Set 'dry_run' to see the plan without doing anything. | =directory= | string | no | Exact root-relative directory, overriding para/category |
| =tags= | string | no | Comma-separated tags |
| =type= | string | no | Summary template: auto, general, meeting, book, youtube, ... |
| =prompt= | string | no | Extra summary instructions |
| =principle= | boolean | no | File it as a principle |

| =sanitize= | string | no | 't' for the default redaction rules, or a comma list of rule names |
| =title= | string | no | Title to use instead of the material's own |
| =name= | string | no | File name seed |
| =format= | string | no | Format of text: org, markdown, text, json, csv, html |
| =crawl= | boolean | no | Follow the links of a web page |
| =depth= | integer | no | How many links deep to crawl |
| =max_pages= | integer | no | Most pages a crawl may fetch |
| =append= | boolean | no | Append to an existing note of the same name |
| =link= | boolean | no | false to skip related notes Default: t. |
| =keep_source= | boolean | no | Copy the original beside the note |

| =text= | string | no | The text, for a text clip |
| =duration_frames= | integer | no | Length in frames (default 90) |
| =r= | integer | no | Red 0-255, for a solid clip (default 128) |
| =g= | integer | no | Green 0-255, for a solid clip (default 128) |
| =b= | integer | no | Blue 0-255, for a solid clip (default 128) |

* web

** web_lql

Run an LQL query on the libresearch metasearch server and return the rows. LQL is a pipeline over search results, e.g. `search "glib", category: CODE | filter extra.stars > 100 | fields title, url' or the shorthand `gtk docs | filter site("docs.gtk.org")'. With explain, return the plan without running it. Use web_research instead for a plain question.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool web lql=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =query= | string | yes | The LQL query |
| =explain= | boolean | no | Plan the query without running it |

** web_research

Research a question on the web and return a cited answer. A libresearch server searches, reads the most relevant pages and answers with numbered citations [n], followed by the sources it cites (title and URL). Use it for questions that need current or external facts; cite the sources you rely on. Slow: a run takes one to several minutes, longer with deep.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool web research=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =question= | string | yes | The question to answer, as a full sentence |
| =deep= | boolean | no | Let the server run follow-up searches (slower, more thorough) |
| =pages= | integer | no | Pages to read, 1-20; omit for the server's default |

** web_search_show

Open a libresearch web search in a results grid in the user's editor, for the USER to read, sort, mark and act on. Returns at once; it does not return the results to you (use web_research or web_lql for that). Use it when the user asks to see or browse search results.

- CLI :: =emacsctl tool web search-show=
- Surfaces :: mcp, dbus, cli, menu, agents
- Returns :: string

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|----------+------+----------+-------------|
| =query= | string | yes | What to search for |
| =category= | string | no | A category: general, news, code, science, it, ... |
